what_its_for: Palbociclib is a cancer medicine used to treat a certain type of breast cancer in adults. It is used for hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. It is usually taken together with another hormone-based medicine. It works by slowing or stopping cancer cells from growing and dividing.
how_to_take: Take palbociclib by mouth with food at the same time every day. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or open them. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another dose that day. Just take your next scheduled dose the following day. Take it exactly as your doctor tells you.
dosing: The usual dose is 125 mg once a day for 21 days in a row, followed by 7 days off (no pills). This 28-day cycle is then repeated. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Never change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store palbociclib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of palbociclib in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid taking herbal supplements like St. John's Wort, as it may make palbociclib less effective. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with palbociclib. Avoid becoming pregnant while on this medicine — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience any of the following: signs of a low white blood cell count such as fever (temperature of 100.4°F or higher), chills, or signs of infection; unusual bruising or bleeding; severe tiredness or weakness; shortness of breath; mouth sores that are painful or severe; signs of a blood clot such as swelling, redness, or pain in your leg; or if you think you may be pregnant. Also call your doctor if you have any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Palbociclib does not cure cancer, but it is designed to slow cancer growth and help you feel better for longer. You may not feel any different right away, but the medicine is working in the background. Your doctor will do regular blood tests and scans to check how well the treatment is working. It may take weeks to months before your doctor can tell if it is helping.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use palbociclib if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. Men: Men with female partners who could become pregnant should use condoms during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, your doctor may adjust your dose. Kidney problems: Dose adjustments are generally not needed for kidney problems, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Older adults: Older adults may take palbociclib safely, but should be watched closely for side effects.
